hook_text: A chair, a plug and a bottle. All plastic, all different, and none of them chosen by accident.
clip_script: Plastics are long chain molecules in two families. Thermoplastics have chains side by side that slide when hot, so they soften, mould and remelt: bottles, bags, chairs, pipes, everything with a recycling code. Thermosets have chains bonded into a net, so they never melt, only char: plugs, pot handles, melamine trays. Their profile: light, tough, bendy, do not conduct electricity or heat, do not rust, mould into anything. Weak in heat, sunlight and fire. So match the job. Clear and strong, PET bottle. Bendy, LDPE bag. Tough outdoors, polypropylene with a UV stabiliser. Stays hard when hot, thermoset plug. Look at any object and ask what it must do, and the plastic answers.
visual_style: Whiteboard spaghetti chains sliding under a flame versus a net chain charring; a property list with icons; four objects each labelled with the property that chose them.
mood: Curious and brisk, like sorting a shop shelf.
pacing: Chains, two families, profile, weaknesses, four matches.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and pick three plastic objects in your home and name the property that chose each.
